headings.title: SMTO-LLM-0046 — The model server sent back an error instead of a reply

html:
SMTO-LLM-0046 — The model server sent back an error instead of a reply

GUID: 79bff8af-c70b-45df-bc82-2e80f3c29186
Slug: model-response-missing
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • SMTO asked the model for its next step, but the model server sent back an error or an empty response instead of an answer. SMTO didn't act on it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, expand Main, and select Check saved model. This shows whether the model server answers normal requests right now.
  2. If it fails, make sure the model server is running, still has the model loaded, and hasn't run out of memory or of its paid usage allowance. Servers return an error instead of a reply when they are overloaded, out of credit, or the model was unloaded.
  3. If the Run stopped, read its activity in the conversation to see which steps already finished, then ask the Agent to continue only the rest. The error reply was not acted on, but earlier steps stay done, so repeating them could do the same work twice.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports passing checks, and the Agent replies to your follow-up.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the model server or manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to redo steps that already finished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model response was not an object or carried a provider error member, so it contained no successful choice to normalize.

What this means

  • Normalization requires a response object without a provider error member; an absent object or error payload supplies no successful decision. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Normalization requires a response object without a provider error member; an absent object or error payload supplies no successful decision.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the response status and typed provider diagnostic before inspecting assistant content; separate service rejection from response-format failure.

How to fix it

  • Raised by normalize_response in src/agent_runtime/llm/openai_compat/response.py and validate_envelope in native_protocol.py. Read the provider error in the trace's provider_diagnostic and the inference server logs, restore the endpoint (model loaded, authentication, quota, memory), and verify with Check saved model before continuing; do not replay completed operations.
  • Inspect the provider’s safe status and protocol diagnostics and restore the served model endpoint before another decision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The endpoint returns a successful response object that passes the normal decision validator.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
